title: GAACA Network Configuration Sample Metadata
description: Per-configuration metadata sidecar for the GAACA Multi-Vendor Network Config Dataset. Every .conf file has a matching .meta.json file following this schema.

product.description: Specific product line or model family

device_class.description: Physical/product asset class (What is the device?)

network_role.description: Operational deployment role (How is the device used?)

routing_capability.description: Whether device has Layer 3 routing capabilities enabled

l3_capable.description: Whether device hardware supports Layer 3 routing

routing_protocols.description: Active routing protocols configured (e.g. BGP, OSPF, ISIS, STATIC)

ambiguity.description: Whether configuration syntax is ambiguous regarding device class

source_url.description: URL of public source if applicable, null for synthetic

license.description: License of source material, null for synthetic

security_state.description: Security posture classification of this configuration sample

security_state_details.description: Brief explanation of what makes this config secure, misconfigured, or edge-case

controls_present.description: Security controls explicitly configured in this sample

controls_absent.description: Security controls deliberately absent or disabled

vulnerability_tags.description: Tags for specific vulnerabilities present (for misconfigured/edge_case)

contains_secrets.description: Always false — no real credentials in this dataset

anonymized.description: Always true — all IPs use RFC 5737 ranges, all secrets are placeholder tokens

generation_date.description: ISO 8601 date when this sample was generated

generator_version.description: Version of the generator script that produced this sample

legacy_device_type.description: Original single-label device_type, preserved verbatim when the separated model was introduced. Retained for auditability.

device_class.description: HARDWARE family. Independent of how the device is deployed. An L3 switch performing a core routing role is still device_class=network_switch.

network_role.description: DEPLOYMENT role. This is what the original device_type was often actually describing when it said 'router'.

platform.description: Operating system / firmware family (Level 1 product identity)

model.description: Identified hardware model, null when the configuration does not name it

capabilities.description: What the configuration proves the device can do. BGP lives here, NOT in device_class.

routing_protocols.description: Subset of capabilities that are routing protocols

l2_capable.description: Derived from capabilities. True when layer-2 forwarding constructs are present.

detected_vendor.description: Vendor family as fingerprinted from the configuration text

device_class_basis.description: Why this device_class was assigned (model registry / defining construct / filename / vendor prior)

label_confidence.description: verified = derived class agrees with the original label; review = they disagree and label_disagreement explains why; ambiguous = the configuration does not uniquely identify a hardware class

relabel_version.description: Version of relabel_dataset.py that produced the separated labels

relabel_date.description: ISO 8601 date the separated labels were written
